title: Answer timings classify insomnia-questionnaire labels in a student cohort
summary: Learned classifiers used the time taken to answer seven questionnaire items to distinguish concurrent insomnia-symptom score labels. Repeated internally balanced evaluations reported an AUROC of 0.824 for raw timings. This is agreement with a self-report scale, not an insomnia diagnosis or a forecast.

source_review.scope: Original primary front;Sections2.1–2.7,3.4–3.5 and4;current primary bibliographic status metadata

evidence.ai_role: Logistic regression and a multilayer perceptron learned a mapping from seven response durations to the concurrent ISI score threshold; model interpretation assessed derived timing features.
evidence.tested: A 2,729-student screening cohort supplied questionnaire timings. Ten random balanced samples each contained141 symptom-positive and141 symptom-negative participants, evaluated with10-fold cross-validation. Raw-timing logistic regression and MLP each reported AUROC0.824.
evidence.unknown: Reference labels are ISI scores of at least8, not independent clinical interviews. The same questionnaire supplied timing features and reference scores. Model comparison and first-fold tuning do not establish a fully nested evaluation; preprocessing and feature selection containment are incomplete. The source reports inconsistent final participant denominators, and balanced resampling does not establish population predictive values. The single-university setting and uncontrolled device/environment effects limit generalization; prospective utility is unestablished.
